Retrieves comprehensive accounting overview data for a claim,
    including claim-level overview, exposure-level overviews, and total summaries.
    This endpoint provides financial data for reserves, payments, incurred amounts,
    recoveries, and net incurred calculations. Uses pagination for exposure data.

    Permissions
    -----------
    Requires read access to at least one of:
        - 'britecore/claims/exposures'
        - 'britecore/claims/accounting'
        - 'agent/claims'

    Parameters
    ----------
    claim_id : str
        The ID of the claim for which to retrieve accounting overview data.
    page : int, optional
        The page number for paginated exposures (default: 1).
    page_size : int, optional
        The number of exposures per page (default: 100).

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        {
            'claim_level_overview': {
                'total_reserve': float,      # Always 0.0 at claim level
                'total_payment': float,      # Always 0.0 at claim level
                'total_incurred': float,     # Always 0.0 at claim level
                'total_recovery': float,     # Sum of all recovery reserves + recovered amounts
                'net_incurred': float        # total_incurred - total_recovery (always negative)
            },
            'exposure_level_overview': [
                {
                    'id': str,                    # Exposure/claim item UUID
                    'claimant_name': str|null,    # Name of the claimant
                    'coverage_name': str,         # Insurance coverage name
                    'loss_name': str,             # Description of the loss/damage
                    'overview': {
                        'total_reserve': float,    # Sum of loss, legal, and adjusting reserves
                        'total_payment': float,    # Sum of all payments made
                        'total_incurred': float,   # total_reserve + total_payment
                        'total_recovery': float,   # Sum of recovery reserves + recovered amounts
                        'net_incurred': float      # total_incurred - total_recovery
                    }
                },
                ...
            ],
            'total_overview': {
                'total_reserve': float,      # Sum of all exposure reserves
                'total_payment': float,      # Sum of all exposure payments
                'total_incurred': float,     # total_reserve + total_payment
                'total_recovery': float,     # Sum of all recovery data (claim + exposure level)
                'net_incurred': float        # total_incurred - total_recovery
            },
            'total_records': int            # Total number of exposures for pagination
        }

Runs the property lookup integration for a property, and stores updates.

    Parameters
    ----------
    property_id : str, required
        The UUID of an existing Property
    integration_instance_id : str, optional
        The UUID of an existing IntegrationInstance to use for the lookup
    dependencies : list, optional
        A list of integration dependencies to store, property items categories and user inputs to store and use on
        the integration lookup call
            - category: str; optional if label is present
                The name of the category if dependency is category.
            - label: str; optional if category is present
                The name of the user input label if dependency is user input.
            - itemId: str; optional
                The ID of the item. If not provided, the value will be stored across all the property items with
                the same name as the category or user input label.
            - value: str; required
                The value to store for the category or user input.
    headless : bool or str, optional
        If True or a string (one of PropertyLookupOptions), this API will not require an integration instance,
        and will execute all the integrations instances with the option enabled (if passed a string).
        If False (default), the API will require an integration instance, and only execute that integration instance.

    Returns
    -------
    success : bool
        True if successful, false if not
    messages : list of str
        List of human-readable messages describing either error or lookup effects
    data : dict
        Indicate which sections have received the update, so that UI can trigger refresh.
        The data response having the form:
        ::
            {
                "rating_information_updates": [{
                    "visible_on_admin_builder": True/False,
                    "visible_on_agent_builder": True/False,
                    "property_item_id": str,
                    "policy_type_item_id": str,
                    "policy_type_item_name": str,
                    "policy_type_item_sort_order": int,
                    "field_name": str,
                    "field_sort_order": int,
                    "old_value": Union[str, None],
                    "new_value": str,
                    "old_value_display": Union[str, None],
                    "new_value_display": str,
                    "type": str,  # "category" or "userInput"
                }, ...],
                "property_information_updates": {
                    "property_value": str,
                    "replacement_cost_value": str,
                },
                "alert_message": str,  # empty string if none
            }

Retrieve Claim Change Log entries.

    Parameters
    ----------
    filter_by : str, required
        The date field to filter by. One of the following:
            'date_stamp' - The date the change was made (in CST timezone).
            Supports time-based filtering if 'allow_timestamp' is set to True.
            'date_cursor' - The calculated date in effect. This typically equals to the date_stamp, except that:
                - It might be NULL when transaction=loss_date;
                - It might be different from date_stamp when transaction=status and changed_to is 'Closed', reflecting
            Does not support time-based filtering.
    from_date : str, required
        The start date of the search.
        If allow_timestamp is True, includes the start time (format YYYY-mm-dd or YYYY-mm-dd HH:MM:SS)
    to_date : str, required
        The end date of the search.
        If allow_timestamp is True, includes the end time (format YYYY-mm-dd or YYYY-mm-dd HH:MM:SS)
    allow_timestamp : bool, optional
        If True and 'filter_by' is set to 'date_stamp', the 'from_date' and 'to_date' arguments
        will be treated as datetime with format 'YYYY-mm-dd HH:MM:SS'.
        If False or not provided, or if 'filter_by' is 'date_cursor', the 'from_date' and 'to_date'
        arguments will be treated as date with format 'YYYY-mm-dd'.
    transactions : list of str, optional
        Limit the search to the specified transactions. Possible values include:
            {'policy', 'status', 'loss_date', 'loss_cause', 'loss_address', 'date_reported',
            'adjuster', 'claimant', 'active', 'coverage',
            'loss_reserve', 'adjustment_reserve', 'legal_reserve', 'claim_payment', 'transaction'}
    policy_type_ids : list of str, optional
        Limit the search to the specified policy types, based on the revision the claim is linked to.
    claim_ids : list of str, optional
        Limit the search to the specified claims

    Returns
    -------
    success : bool
        True if successful, False if not
    data : dict
        Contains claim change log info
    message : str
        Human-readable messages

This endpoint returns a comprehensive list of all accounting transactions associated with a specific claim.
    The transactions include:

    - **Payments**: Loss, adjusting, and legal payments made against the claim
    - **Reserves**: Loss, adjusting, and legal reserves established for the claim
    - **Recoveries**: Reinsurance, subrogation, salvage, and reinsurance LAE recoveries
    - **Recovery Reserves**: Reserves established for potential recoveries

    Transactions are sorted by date in descending order (most recent first) and include detailed
    information about exposures, payees, and payment methods.
    This endpoint uses pagination to return the data.

    Permissions
    -----------
    Requires read access to at least one of:
        - 'britecore/claims/accounting'
        - 'agent/claims'
    Parameters
    ----------
    claim_id : str
        The ID of the claim for which to retrieve transactions data.
    page : int, optional
        The page number for paginated exposures (default: 1).
    page_size : int, optional
        The number of exposures per page (default: 100).

    Returns
    -------
    success : bool
        True if successful, false if not
    messages : list of str
        Human-readable messages.
    data : dict
        Contains the transactions objects in the following format. Some fields could be missing if not relevant ::
            {
                'transactions': [
                    {
                        'id': str,
                        'transaction_type': str,
                        'transaction_category': str,
                        'amount': Decimal,
                        'new_amount': Decimal,
                        'previous_amount': Decimal,
                        'exported': bool,
                        'exported_datetime': datetime,
                        'voided': bool,
                        'voided_datetime': datetime,
                        'transaction_datetime': datetime,
                        'modified_by_username': str,
                        'description': str,
                        'memo': str,
                        'recovery_category': str,
                        'contact_id': str,
                        'address_id': str,
                        'exposure_id': str,
                        'payee_ids': list of str,
                        'payment_classification': str,
                        'payment_method_account_name': str,
                        'payment_method_masked_number': str,
                        'payment_method': str,
                        'payees': [
                            {
                                'id': str,
                                'name': str
                            },
                            ...
                        ],
                        'modified_by': str,
                        'claim_level_transaction': bool,
                        'exposure_details': {
                            'id': str,
                            'claimant_name': str,
                            'coverage_name': str,
                            'loss_name': str,
                            'reinsurance_reserve': Decimal,
                            'reinsurancelae_reserve': Decimal,
                            'salvage_reserve': Decimal,
                            'subrogation_reserve': Decimal
                        }
                    },
                    ...
                ],
                "total_records": int
            }

    Parameters
    ----------
    revision_id : uuid
        Required. The database identifier of the revision for which a deliverable should be generated
    deliverable_type : str
        Required. The name of the deliverable that should be generated

        Effective date for the deliverable (bill date, print date, etc.)
    reference_type : str
        Either 'policies' or 'claims', depending on the type of deliverable being requested
    proc_date : str
        Date that will be recorded as the generation date of the deliverable
    location_id : uuid
        Specifies the business location whose version of the requested deliverable should be generated
        (were multiple copies of like-named deliverables to exist). Can differ from the specified revision's
        location at the caller's own risk. If not specified, will be inferred to be the location of the
        specified revision
    invoice_id : uuid
        For deliverables that utilize a "last invoice" for content population, serves as an override to
        render off a known invoice's data
    reason : str
        Reason for generating a deliverable. Can have an impact on print date, based on deliverable type
    claim_number : str
        Number of the claim that should be used for populating the content of the requested deliverable
    return_premium_id : uuid
        For deliverables that utilize a "return premium" for content population, serves as an override to
        render off a known return premium's data
    filepath : str
        Filepath under which the new deliverable should be stored
    claim_id : uuid
        Database identifier of the claim that should be used for populating the content of the requested
        deliverable
    claim_loss_date : str
        For deliverables that utilize a "loss date" for content population, serves as that value
    delay_print_days : int
        Number of days that the print date should be delayed from its typical assignment
    print_state : str
        Print state to be given to the deliverable

    Returns
    -------
    success : bool
        Whether or not the deliverable was generated
    messages : list of str
        List of human-readable success or error messages
    data : dict
        An object of the following format, pointing to the location of the folder containing the
        generated deliverable.

        Whether contact is isGod or not. Defaults to 'False'. (Note: Only isGod users can set this to 'True')

        List of roles that contact has.

        The username of the contact.

    confirmation_email : str
        The unique email used for log in.

        ::

            {
                "alert_email": "test@email.com",
                "alert_status": "true",
                "month": "03",
                "day": "01",
                "year": "2023",
                "contents": "A reminder note",
                "frequency": "This Date Only",
                "alert_time_period": "2",
                "alert_time_unit": "Day/s",
                "touchpoint": "",
            }

    position : str
        Position for an individual contact.

    name_aliases : list[str]
        A list of name aliases

    company: str
        The company contact uuid.

    organization_contacts : list
        A list of contact ids belonging to this organization.

    agency_administrators : list
        A list of contact ids as agency administrator for this organization.

    related_to : list
        A list of related contacts. The related contact must either not linked to any policy,
        or shares the same set of policies with this contact.

        If true, duplicate copy from contact info to all related contacts.

    Parameters
    ----------
    policy_number : str
        defaults to the next system generated policy number

        defaults to today
    term_type : str
        ('Custom', '3 Years', '18 Months', '1 Year', '9 Months', '6 Months', '3 Months')
    expiration_date : str
        (optional) - required if term_type is 'Custom'
    renewal_term_type : str
        ('3 Years', '18 Months', '1 Year', '9 Months', '6 Months', '3 Months')

        (optional) if the policy should be processed as a renewal
    underwriting_questions : list
        (optional) if enforcing underwriting questions
    underwriting_options : list
        (optional) if enforcing underwriting options
    as_agent : bool
        If true, creator and agent relations are based on logged in user
        It also adds a meta key in the response that holds the redirect_uri location
        of the new quote.
    manual_policy_number : bool
        indicates whether the policy number was manually assigned
    policy_type_id : uuid
        (optional): Given a policy type ID, the policy type is attached to the revision
    effective_date : str
        (optional) - required if effective_date is different than inception_date. Defaults to inception date
    external_system_reference : str
    property_zip : str
        (optional) - used to determine if there are suspensions for this zip code.

    Returns
    -------
    success : bool
        True if successful, false if not

        List of human-readable error messages

        The data response having the form:
        ::

             'revision_data': {*see retrieve_revision_details*}

    Parameters
    ----------
    data : str, required
        A string representation of a csv file. Entries should map agency_number
        to a respective amount used to create a commission payment record.
        Agency numbers can appear more than once on the input csv, and must
        refer to one and only one contact (i.e. an agency number cannot be used
        on the csv if two contacts can be reached by this number). Any value
        convertible to a python float is acceptable., including 0.

        Example 1 (with csv header row):
            agency_number,amount
            T34514,11207.12
            T34515,15000.00
            T34516,12120.55
            T34514,720.00
            T34516,720.00

List STP (Straight-Through Processing) execution results for a revision with pagination.

    Retrieves all STP rule execution instances and their individual rule results
    for a specific revision, ordered by execution date descending.

    Parameters
    ----------
    params : dict
        A JSON object containing request parameters. Required fields include:
        - `revision_id` : str : UUID of the revision to get STP results for.
        Optional fields include:
        - `page` : int : Page number for pagination (default: 1).
        - `page_size` : int : Number of executions per page, max 100 (default: 25).

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        A JSON object containing paginated STP execution results:
        - `results` : list : Array of STP execution objects, each containing:
            - `id` : str : UUID of the STP execution.
            - `revision_id` : str : UUID of the associated revision.
            - `execution_start_time` : str : ISO datetime when execution started.
            - `execution_end_time` : str : ISO datetime when execution ended.
            - `status` : str : Overall execution status ('success' or 'error').
            - `total_rules_executed` : int : Total number of rules executed.
            - `total_rules_succeeded` : int : Number of rules that succeeded.
            - `total_rules_failed` : int : Number of rules that failed.
            - `results` : list : Array of individual rule execution results, each containing:
                - `id` : str : UUID of the rule result.
                - `rule_name` : str : Name of the executed rule.
                - `rule_severity` : str or null : Severity level of the rule ('critical', 'high', 'medium', 'low') or null if not set.
                - `status` : str : Rule execution status ('success' or 'error').
                - `error_description` : str or null : Error details if rule failed.
                - `custom_error_code_id` : str or null : Associated custom error code ID.
                - `custom_error_code` : dict or null : Custom error code details if available, containing:
                    - `id` : str : UUID of the custom error code.
                    - `module` : str : Error code module (e.g., 'stp').
                    - `code` : str : Error code string.
                    - `description` : str : Error description.
                - `property_id` : str or null : Property ID if rule is property-specific.
                - `driver_contact_id` : str or null : Driver contact ID if rule is driver-specific.
        - `pagination` : dict : Pagination metadata containing:
            - `page` : int : Current page number.
            - `page_size` : int : Number of items per page.
            - `total_count` : int : Total number of executions.
            - `total_pages` : int : Total number of pages.

Please use api/v2/payments/store_external_payment endpoint if you're simply registering an external payment.

    For given invoice/policy number we identify it's respective policy and primary payment method,
    to then apply the respective amount on the payment_date. System uses the auto-pay payment method,
    but if non located it will default to the primary insureds' first payment method.

    - Payments are always invoked through PaymentController().make_payment(). When payment_transaction_id is set, it's
    assumed funds are already deducted any payment recorded would have similar effects as a "Cash" (but instead of
    payment type cash, shows as respective payment vendor). Other information such as payor name and an identifier
    to track the source of the payment are also optionally captured for tracking purposes.

    - `payment_transaction_id` and `source_id` and `meta` are mandatory when recording a payment that has already
    happened.


    Parameters
    ----------
    amount : float
        amount payment was recoded as.
    payment_date : str, optional
        date in format 'YYYY-MM-dd' representing when payment was made.
    invoice_number : str
        AccountHistory.id (UUID) for invoice for respective policy term payment
        was made against.
    policy_number : str, optional
        Policy.policy_number of the account we want to make payment on.
    payment_transaction_id : str, optional
        The transaction reference id for the payment.
    source_id : str, optional
        A string identifier that shows where the payment originates from.
    meta: object: dict, optional
        An object containing payment metadata.
        ::
            {
                'payorName': <string>,
                'maskedNumber': <string>, # Last four of ACH account or CC number
                'payment_method': <string>, # One of Visa, MC, AMEX, Discover, ACH
            }

    Returns
    -------
    success : True if payment processed correctly, otherwise false
    messages : list of failure messages
        ::
            [
                'Attempted to setup default payment method',
                'Updated account balance'  # present if success payment was processed'
            ]
    data : dict
        ::
            {
                'isDuplicate': false,
                'payoffAmount': <decimal>,  # overall amount due to payoff policy term
                'confirmationNumber': "124312312",  # numeric string value that can be used to nsf payment later
            }

Get all the deliverables and associated deliverables to print.

    This is a sane, backwards incompatible re-implementation of retrieveToBePrinted.

    Arguments:
        from_date : The earliest date to retrieve files from. Should be formatted
                   like "YYYY-MM-DD". Defaults to the client's live date.
        to_date : The latest date to retrieve files from. Should be formatted
                 like "YYYY-MM-DD". Defaults to today's date.
        ignore_state : (optional) Ignore the file's print state. Defaults to False.
        exclude_electronic_delivery : Default False, excludes documents that should
                                     be delivered electronically.
        only_electronic_delivery : Default False, only returns documents that should
                                  be delivered electronically.
        include_claims : Default False, if passed as true any claim deliverables
                        with tbd print state get returned within the same batch.
                        fields for claim deliverables are exactly the same for policy.
        disable_edelivery_filtering : Default False, if passed as true no edelivery
                                     filtering will occur
        include_address_fields : Default False, if passed as true the address fields
                                will be included in the output

    Returns:
        An JSON string containing an object with two members, consistent ordering
        not guaranteed:

           processing: Whether or not nightly processing for the to_date
                         is processing, done, or not started.
           files: A list of objects with the policy number, file id, date it
                  should print, label, and title, parent id or children ids.
                  For example:

                    {'processing': 'done',
                    'files': [{'policy_number': '10-2013-42',
                                'file_id': 'f6b8f1b0-e4b0-4738-b96d-51c270c76580',
                                'contact_id': 'c4e448ea-6494-439f-94eb-829a05f8f9f2',
                                'print_date': '2013-05-21',
                                'print_state': 'tbd',
                                'label': 'Declaration',
                                'title': '10-2013-42 - Declaration',
                                'batch': page_range(1,5)},
                            {'policy_number': '10-2013-42',
                                'file_id': '774f0b38-2b49-4d7c-ae0f-19541841fbeb',
                                'contact_id': 'c7404bb5-3d07-43c1-bc7b-2caffde84330',
                                'print_date': '2013-05-21',
                                'print_state': 'tbd',
                                'label': null,
                                'title': 'form-m01a32ll.pdf',
                                'parent': 'f6b8f1b0-e4b0-4738-b96d-51c270c76580',
                                'batch': ''}
                             ]
                    }

                  To retrieve the file, the file_id item of each object in the list
                  can be passed to core.uploads.getAttachment as the GET parameter "id".

    # This should be in a wiki article or other client-facing documentation
    Developer Reference For Using the BritePrint API:

      * A normal day's job consists of simply fetching the result of getToBePrinted,
        downloading the files, printing them as desired, and then marking them as
        printed in BriteCore to prevent duplicate print jobs. The result SHOULD be
        parsed as JSON.

      * The "processing" member should be checked for the value "done". Any other value
        indicates that processing for today is either "incomplete" or "not started".
        Implementations SHOULD wait until that value becomes "done" before starting a
        day's printing to ensure all files needing to be printed for that day are listed.

      * The "files" member contains an array of objects, one for each file.
        Stable ordering is not guaranteed, though it should be correct for most use-cases.

      * The "policy_number" member in the file object may be used to group and
        sort the files by policy number.

      * The "revision_id" member in the file object may be used to group and sort
        the files by revision id.

      * The "file_id" member contains the id to send to the getAttachment method
        in BriteCore.

      * The "contact_id" member contains the BriteCore contact id of the recipient.

      * The "print_date" member may be used to sort by the file's desired print date.

      * The "print_state" member is a hint as to whether or not the file has been
        printed or not. Possible values are:
            - "tbd" (to be determined, that is, not printed yet)
            - "do not print" (Never print this.)
            - "printed" (already printed at least once.)
            - "failed" (marked as a failed print job.)
            - "void"
            - "silenced"
            - "sent"
            - "not mailed"

      * The "label" member is the type of document. For example, "Declaration" or
        "Notice of Cancellation". For forms, this is null.

      * The "title" member is the document's title. For regular deliverables, it will
        usually be the policy number and label. For forms, this might be something
        like "form-m01a3dll.pdf" or "C0A63".

      * The "parent" member indicates that this file should be printed in addition to
        its parent. This is for additional forms for Declarations, for example.
        This will not be present if there is no parent document.

      * The "children" member indicates that this file is a composite of the documents
        listed under that key.

      * The "batch" member indicates the batch, if any, that this document was classified
        under by `merge_mailings`. This will always be empty for forms (if parent is present)
        or if the `merge_docs_by_recipient_and_pol` setting is not in use.

      * Sometimes print jobs get backlogged, for example, over weekends or holidays.

      * After sorting the deliverables as desired, you should pull down the PDF files
        themselves by calling getAttachment, and passing it the file_id of a file.
        From there, it can be printed as desired.

      * After they've been sent to the printer, you MUST call markAsPrinted with the
        file_ids of the files you've printed. Failing to do so can result in processing
        errors later, and will not cause the file to appear in the list of files when
        reprinting later.

    If applicable, a relationship is set up between a given revision
    and the contact.

    Parameters
    ----------
    role : string
        Optional. The name of the role to add the new contact to. Example: 'Agent'.
    content : dict
        Required. The following keys are expected:
            {
                'name': str,
                'type': str,
                'confirmationEmail': str,
                'legalEntityType': str,
                'website': str,
                'username': str,
                'isGod': boolean,
                'cognitoUsername': str,
                'dba': '2020-04-14',
                'purchaseDate': '2020-04-14',
                'riskIdNumber': str,
                'agencyId': UUID,
                'stateId': UUID,
                'licenseNumber': str,
                'ssn': 'str',
                'addedBy': str,
                'roles': [str],

                # Date of birth can be set via following 3 keys
                'dobMonth': '04',
                'dobYear': '2020',
                'dobDay': '14',
                # Alternatively, can be set directly via following key in the given format
                'dob': '2020-04-14',

                # Date business started can be set via following 3 keys
                'dbsYear': '2020',
                'dbsMonth': '04',
                'dbsDay': '14',
                # Alternatively, can be set directly via following key in the given format
                'dbs': '2020-04-14',
                # Or via following key
                'dateBusinessStarted': '2020-04-14',

                # Agency inception/termination date can be set via following 3 keys
                'agencyInceptionDateYear': '2019',
                'agencyInceptionDateMonth': '02',
                'agencyInceptionDateDay': '03',
                'agencyTerminationDateYear': '2020',
                'agencyTerminationDateMonth': '05',
                'agencyTerminationDateDay': '06',
                # Or directly via following key in the given format
                'agencyInceptionDate': '2019-02-03',
                'agencyTerminationDate': '2020-05-06',

                # Either of the following keys can be used to set FeinTax
                'feinTaxId': str,
                'feinTax': str,

                # following key can be alternatively passed as 'emails'
                'emailAddresses': [
                    {
                        'email': str,
                        # following key can be alternatively passed as 'type'
                        'emailType': str
                    }
                ],

                # following key can be alternatively passed as 'phones'
                'phoneNumbers': [
                    {
                        'email': str,
                        # following key can be alternatively passed as 'type'
                        'phoneType': str
                    }
                ],

                'addresses': [
                    {
                        'addressLine1': str,
                        'addressCity': str,
                        'addressState': str,
                        'addressZip': str,
                        'addressCountry': str,
                        'addressCityOther': str,   # optional when country is not USA/Canada
                        'addressCountyOther': str, # optional when country is not USA/Canada
                        'addressStateOther': str,  # optional when country is not USA/Canada
                        'addressStateCanada': str, # optional when address provider is not google

                        # following key can be alternatively passed as 'type'
                        'addressType': str

                    }
                ],
            }

    Returns
    -------
    success : bool
        Whether or not the contact could be created.
    id : UUID
        Id of the newly created contact
    address_ids : list of UUID
        List containing id of created addresses

            "items_added": bool,  // Indicate if any mandatory builder items were added because agency billing was unset
            "updated_rating_items": {  // Optional. Contain details of the builder items after the update,

Update edelivery_documents

    Parameters
    ----------
    records : dict of dicts
        records need to be updated. Format is
        ::
            {
                # UUID of e-deliverable_document entity
                "ef763124-8b7f-4016-ac54-7d07e4adfe70": {
                    # desired state. One of unprocessed/pending/processed. Flags internal state of e-delivery
                    "state": "pending"
                },
                "ef763124-8b7f-4016-ac54-7d07e4adfe71": {  # UUID of e-deliverable_document entity
                    "state": "processed",                  # desired state. One of unprocessed/pending/processed
                    # if set to true - document will be excluded from printing queue (except certifieds)
                    "exclude_from_printing_queue": True
                },
                "ef763124-8b7f-4016-ac54-7d07e4adfe72": {  # UUID of e-deliverable_document entity
                    "state": "processed",                  # desired state. One of unprocessed/pending/processed
                    # if set to true - document will be excluded from printing queue (except certifieds)
                    "exclude_from_printing_queue": False,
                    # reflects state of e-delivery. Required to inform BC users about E-DElivery state of document
                    "edelivery_state": "FAILED"
                },
                "ef763124-8b7f-4016-ac54-7d07e4adfe73": {  # UUID of e-deliverable_document entity
                    "state": "processed",                  # desired state. One of unprocessed/pending/processed
                    # if set to true - document will be excluded from printing queue (except certifieds)
                    "exclude_from_printing_queue": False,
                    # reflects state of e-delivery. Required to inform BC users about E-DElivery state of document
                    "edelivery_state": "NOTIFIED",
                    # if set to true - document will be excluded from printing queue (certifieds)
                    "exclude_certified_from_printing_queue": False
                }
            }

    Returns
    -------
    success : bool
        True if successful, false if not
    messages : list of str
        List of human-readable error messages
    data: dict
        Dict with update results (true or false)
        ::
            {
                'ef763124-8b7f-4016-ac54-7d07e4adfe70': True,
                'ef763124-8b7f-4016-ac54-7d07e4adfe71': False
            }

Finds all active files for a specific entity, given a reference point. Optionally can retrieve files
    with a NULL reference object as well (example, Report files). Additional filters can also be applied
    if desired.

    Parameters
    ----------
    reference_id : str
        The UUID of the object reference to which the files are associated.
        If intentionally omitted, `allow_null_reference` is expected,
            or `policy_number`/`claim_number` should be provided.
    policy_number : str
        The policy number, if `reference_id` is unknown but the files are tied to a policy.
    claim_number : str
        The claim number, if `reference_id` is unknown but the files are tied to a claim.
    allow_null_reference : bool
        If the queried files are not tied to a specific entity, pass as True (defaults to False).
        Example: Report result files do not currently have `reference_id` to any given entity.
    ascending : bool
        By default, the resulting list will be ordered by `dateAdded`-descending for most recently created first.
        Pass this in as True to show oldest first.
    advanced_filters : list
        A list of specific dictionaries that expands filtering to a :makevar:`File` by giving
            explicit comparison operators.
        Must have three keys in the dict to accomplish successful filtering and failing to pass any of
        them will result in the given filter being ignored.
        They are :kbd:`column`, :kbd:`operator`, :kbd:`value`

        :column: The column's value in a File table.
        :operator: The comparison operator, have a look at python's built in
                   `operator <https://docs.python.org/2/library/operator.html>`_ package
                   The only allowed operators are :kbd:`lt le eq ne ge gt`
        :value: The value being compared to.
        Below is an example of how an advanced filter dictionary looks like:
        ::
            {
                "column": "label",
                "operator": "ne",
                "value": "Form"
            }
    Returns
    -------
    success : bool
        True if successful, false if not
    messages : list of str
        List of human-readable error messages
    data : list
        The data response having the form:
        ::
            [
                {
                    "id": "UUID",
                    "title": "Declaration - John Smith",
                    "label": "Declaration",
                    "date_added": "2018-01-01 12:00:00",
                    "print_state": "printed",
                    "print_date": "2018-02-01",
                    "actual_print_date": "2018-02-02",
                    "folder_id": "UUID",
                    "mime_type": "application/pdf",
                    "size": 4096,
                    "type": "policies",
                    "sub_type": "New Policy"
                }
            ]

Applies a collection of transaction records as accounted BriteCore
    payments.

    Parameters
    ----------
    transactions : list of dict
        Iterable containing dicts of the following format:
        ::
            {
                # Reference to an existing policy number, cleared of
                # non-numerical characters (ex: the policy "P90-2010-8" would
                # be represented here as "9020108")
                "policy": str,

                # Code identifying the check to be processed.
                "check": str,

                # The amount to be payed (with precision: 0.00).
                "payment": decimal.Decimal,
            }

    Returns
    -------
    success : bool
    messages : list of strings
        List of human readable error messages filled only when success != True.
    data : list of dict
        A list of dicts, containing the results of the individual attempts to
        apply the payment transactions. The result list is aligned to the input
        transactions list, meaning it is possible to zip(transactions, results)
        to analyze the results in respect to its input. Each contained element
        has the following format:
        ::

            {
                # Either "success" when the respective payment was correctly
                # applied or "error" when it was not.
                "result": str,

                # A human readable message detailing the result field in case its
                # value is different from "success".
                "detail": str
            }
